weakness_class: F115 Security controls bypass or absence (client_trusted_value / trusting a less-trusted source for an IP allow-list; CWE-290, CWE-348)
trigger: Request to /anything/** with header X-Forwarded-For set to an IpUtils.WHITE_LISTS entry (e.g. localhost)
exploit_path: IpFilter now reads the client-written X-Forwarded-For header before the TCP peer hostname, so any caller outside the allow-list passes the gate by asserting an allowed hostname; the 401 branch is unreachable for an attacker who sets the header.
notes: Upstream candidate label was rate_limit_key_trust; corrected to control-bypass via client-trusted IP because the control is an allow-list, not a rate-limit key. Route also requires OIDC authentication (SecurityConfiguration), so the bypass is by any authenticated principal.

weakness_class: F115 Security controls bypass or absence (rate_limit_key_trust / trusting a less-trusted source; CWE-348, CWE-770)
trigger: Requests to /headers rotating the X-Real-IP or X-Forwarded-For header value
exploit_path: userRemoteAddressResolver is the only KeyResolver bean, so SCG injects it into RequestRateLimiterGatewayFilterFactory and the /headers RedisRateLimiter (burst 2, replenish 2) buckets by its key; the key now comes from IpUtils.getRealIp, which prefers the client headers, so every distinct header value gets a fresh bucket and one client exceeds the limit indefinitely.
notes: Interprocedural: sink in DemoApplication.userKeyResolver, tainted source in IpUtils.getRealIp (lines 15-31, pre-existing helper previously used only for audit logging). KeyResolver selection verified with javap on spring-cloud-gateway-server-2.2.6 (PrincipalNameKeyResolver is @ConditionalOnMissingBean).

weakness_class: F115 Security controls bypass or absence (absent_control: rate limiting missing on a route to a rate-limited upstream; CWE-770, CWE-799)
exploit_path: The new /api/v1/headers route rewrites the path to the same upstream /headers resource that the /headers route protects with RedisRateLimiter, but its filter chain only has setPath and addRequestHeader; a client that switches to the alias path reaches the upstream at an unbounded rate.
notes: Rendered the upstream hint ('route with a trivial filter and no rate limiter') as an alias route so that the /headers limiter stays live and SCGD-002 remains reachable in the final tree.
